VMARG_LIST="-XX:ParallelGCThreads=2 -XX:CICompilerCount=2 -Djava.awt.headless=true"

# Apply Java options from externally set environment variables
VMARG_LIST="${VMARG_LIST} ${GHIDRA_JAVA_OPTIONS} ${GHIDRA_HEADLESS_JAVA_OPTIONS}"

# DEBUG_ADDRESS set via environment for launch.sh
DEBUG_ADDRESS=${DEBUG_ADDRESS} "${SCRIPT_DIR}"/launch.sh "${LAUNCH_MODE}" jdk Ghidra-Headless "${GHIDRA_HEADLESS_MAXMEM}" "${VMARG_LIST}" ghidra.app.util.headless.AnalyzeHeadless "$@"

# Get the configurable VM arguments from the launch properties
while IFS=$'\r\n' read -r line; do
	VMARGS_FROM_LAUNCH_PROPS+=("$line")
done < <("${JAVA_CMD}" -cp "${LS_CPATH}" LaunchSupport "${INSTALL_DIR}" -vmargs)

else
	set -o noglob; "${JAVA_CMD}" "${VMARGS_FROM_LAUNCH_PROPS[@]}" "${VMARGS_FROM_LAUNCH_SH[@]}" ${VMARGS_FROM_CALLER} -showversion -cp "${CPATH}" ghidra.Ghidra ${CLASSNAME} "${ARGS[@]}"
	exit $?
fi

# The following property will limit the number of processor cores that Ghidra
# will use for thread pools. If not specified, it will use the default number 
# of processors returned from Runtime.getRuntime().getAvailableProcessors(). 
# Otherwise, it will use the min of the value returned from Runtime and the 
# value specified by the following property.
VMARGS=-Dcpu.core.limit=

# The following property is a way to exactly specify the number of processor 
# cores that Ghidra will use for thread pools.  Note: this will supersede the 
# above 'cpu.core.limit' value if it is set.
VMARGS=-Dcpu.core.override=
